walkthroughs.body_html:
Economic Objectives and the Role of Government — a core area of GCSE Economics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Economic Objectives and the Role of Government brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Economic Objectives and the Role of Government.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Changes to interest rates in the UK are decided by:
options: HM Treasury
MPC of the Bank of England
Office for National Statistics
Prime Minister

mcqs.q: Which is a fiscal policy tool?
options: Interest rates
Income tax
Money supply
Exchange rates

mcqs.q: How is economic growth shown on a Production Possibility Curve?
options: Growth is shown by moving from inside the curve to a point on the curve.
By an outward shift of the entire curve — reflecting an increase in productive capacity through more or better resources, technology, or skills.
A Pigouvian tax is a tax only on rich people.
Growth is shown by the curve becoming straighter.

mcqs.q: What defines a pure public good?
options: A public good is anything that's free.
A public good is anything provided by the government.
Non-rivalry (one person's use doesn't reduce others') and non-excludability (you can't stop people benefiting) — e.g. national defence, street lighting.
A Pigouvian tax is a tax only on rich people.
A Pigouvian tax is a tax that funds government spending.
Growth is shown by the curve becoming straighter.
A Pigouvian tax is a tax only on rich people.
A tax set equal to the external cost of an activity — designed to internalise the externality so the private cost reflects the social cost. Used for pollution, congestion, sugary drinks.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Monetary policy”?
options: Transferring state-owned enterprises to private ownership; major UK programme in 1980s under Thatcher.
Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee changes interest rates and uses quantitative easing to control inflation.
Government-owned activities like NHS, state schools and roads; funded by taxation and borrowing.
Rules set by government or regulators (Ofgem, Ofcom) to correct market failure and protect consumers.
